I’m 57, been farming this land for 30 years. My wife and I manage 6 mu — not big, but it’s what we have. We do wheat-maize double crop, same as most folks around here. I didn’t go past primary school, so I don’t know those fancy calculations. I go by what I’ve seen with my own eyes and what the neighbors do.

Last year the wheat did alright — around 400 jin per mu. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then topdressed urea when the wheat was jointing. That’s what I always do, and it works. Old Wang down the road tried to save money on fertilizer two years ago and his wheat turned yellow and thin. I’m not making that mistake. With only two of us, every yuan matters, but a bad harvest hurts more than spending a bit more on fertilizer.

For wheat this year: I’ll plant right after National Day, maybe October 5th or so, using the same seed I saved from last year. Base fertilizer is compound, about one bag per mu. Then at jointing I’ll spread urea — probably 10 kg per mu, maybe 15 if the wheat looks hungry. I’ll irrigate three times: once before winter freeze, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Water costs money, but dry wheat is worthless. For pests, I’ll spray herbicide after planting, and if I see armyworms I’ll get insecticide from the shop.

For maize: plant right after wheat harvest in early June — no time to waste, the window is tight. I buy hybrid seed from the seed shop, about 40 yuan per mu. Maize needs less fuss than wheat. I put compound fertilizer down at planting, then urea at the big flare stage. Two irrigations if it stays dry — one when it’s small, one at flare. Maybe a third if July is scorching. Labor is just me and my wife. Wheat harvest is the worst week — I hire a combine for harvest and a tractor for plowing, maybe 3-4 days total. The rest we do ourselves.

I expect wheat around 400 kg per mu and maize around 450 kg per mu if the weather cooperates. I’m not trying to be the best farmer in the county — I just need enough to live on and a little saved for next year.
